note: What the cross-session stranded-spool sweep (task-spor-nudge-async-cross-session-spool-sweep) would have reached in the corpus the 2026-09-04 replay left indeterminate. This is a COVERAGE measurement of the sweep's evidence channel, NOT a measured production loss reduction: nudge.async is default-off, no `.out.json` has ever existed on this box (there is no journal/pending-nudges dir at all), so every number the replay produces is counterfactual and so is this. It asks one question the replay could not: for each residual `no-sessionend-observed` finding, is its session bound by a TERMINAL dispatch run record — the only evidence this sweep acts on? Method: re-run the pinned replay harness (spor 0f7abae, scripts/analysis/measure-async-nudge-loss.js, same default window), then join each residual finding's session id against journal/dispatch/*.run.json on this box. The replay's own bound is re-quoted below and is UNCHANGED by this work — the sweep adds no historical recovery, since the corpus predates both the mode and the origin record the sweep attributes from.

rerun.drift: 4 pinned rows no longer score — their ~/.claude/projects transcripts have been pruned since 2026-09-04. Nothing disagreed.
rerun.bound_moved_because: transcript eviction shrank the scored corpus, NOT because anything was recovered. Re-pin, do not compare.

evidence_coverage.question: Would the sweep's terminal-evidence door have reached the residual population?
evidence_coverage.reading: 3 of 3 residual sessions (4 of 4 pinned residual findings, 5 of 5 residual facts) are bound by a terminal `done` dispatch record that is STILL on disk a month later, and every one is a native-background dispatch — the population the replay said the residual concentrated in. So the evidence channel this sweep keys on covers the whole residual, which is the structural claim; whether a given finding would then have been CAPTURED still depends on the spool surviving to be swept.
evidence_coverage.why_origin_json_and_not_the_run_record: None of the three records carries `project`, `server` or `org` (a native-background launch stamps them only when the dispatch supplied them), so a run record proves the session ENDED but cannot say which tenant or project its findings belong to. That is why attribution is read from the `origin.json` post-tool now writes beside the spool, and why a legacy spool without one is retained and reported rather than guessed at (dec-spor-stranded-spool-terminal-evidence-policy).

unverified: No end-to-end production recovery is demonstrated: async has never been enabled on this box, so no real stranded spool exists to sweep. The acceptance cases are exercised against synthetic fixtures in test/nudge-sweep.test.js.

The 4 pinned residual findings are INDETERMINATE, not demonstrated losses (art-spor-async-nudge-loss-remeasured-2026-09-04); recovering their sessions' spools would remove an upper bound, not a measured loss.

Evidence has a lifetime: `dispatch.runRetentionMs` (default 14d) prunes terminal records. A spool whose record has aged out reads as `unknown` and is retained. These three records outlived their nominal retention because pruning runs at launch time, not on a timer.
